fanoutqa_017414.x:
Suits (American TV series) :: Series overview :: Season 7 (2017–18) :: chunk_0009
Main article: [Suits season 7](/wiki/Suits_season_7 "Suits season 7")

Everyone at the firm struggles to adjust to Jessica's absence. Donna takes a position as [COO](/wiki/Chief_operating_officer "Chief operating officer"), and Harvey's friend Alex Williams joins the team. Harvey begins dating Paula; Louis' sessions with his own German therapist, Stan Lipschitz, have mixed results. Rachel begins her career as an attorney, having passed the bar. Mike continues to work pro bono cases at the clinic, with Harvey's blessing, but one of the cases puts Alex, Harvey, and others at risk. Louis and Sheila Sasz, Head of Admissions for Columbia University, reconnect, as does [Jessica with her family in Chicago](/wiki/Pearson_(TV_series) "Pearson (TV series)"). Mike and Rachel accept an offer to found and run their own [public interest law](/wiki/Public_interest_law "Public interest law") firm in [Seattle](/wiki/Seattle "Seattle") that takes on [class-action suits](/wiki/Class_action "Class action"), and get married before leaving. As the season closes, a case that puts Specter Litt in danger is the work of top lawyer Robert Zane's partners, Ellen Rand and Eric Kaldor. When Zane finds out, he joins forces with Specter Litt.

During a Week 6 38–33 road loss to the [Arizona Cardinals](/wiki/2017_Arizona_Cardinals_season "2017 Arizona Cardinals season"), Fitzpatrick entered the game after starter [Jameis Winston](/wiki/Jameis_Winston "Jameis Winston") suffered a shoulder injury in the second quarter. > "When you saw him you would think: this kid can't play ball. He's a dwarf, he's too fragile, too small. But immediately you'd realise that he was born different, that he was a phenomenon."

— [Newell's Old Boys](/wiki/Newell%27s_Old_Boys "Newell's Old Boys") youth coach [Adrián Coria](/wiki/Adri%C3%A1n_Coria_(football_manager) "Adrián Coria (football manager)"), sharing his first impression of the 12-year-old Messi[[32]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTECaioli201238-37)

Messi started playing for the [Rosario](/wiki/Rosario "Rosario")-based football club [Newell's Old Boys](/wiki/Newell%27s_Old_Boys "Newell's Old Boys") when he was seven years old; he would become a lifelong supporter of the club. During the six years he played for Newell's, he scored almost 500 goals, and was a member of "The Machine of '87", a nearly unbeatable youth team named for the year of their birth. Messi regularly entertained crowds by performing ball tricks during half-time, when the Newell's [first team](/wiki/Glossary_of_association_football_terms#First_team "Glossary of association football terms") played home games.[[B]](#cite_note-41) His goalscoring idol growing up was Brazilian striker [Ronaldo](/wiki/Ronaldo_(Brazilian_footballer) "Ronaldo (Brazilian footballer)"), who Messi called "the best forward I've ever seen".[[36]](#cite_note-42)

Messi's future as a professional player was threatened when, at the age of 10, he was diagnosed with a [growth hormone deficiency](/wiki/Growth_hormone_deficiency "Growth hormone deficiency"). He began [growth hormone therapy](/wiki/Growth_hormone_therapy "Growth hormone therapy") at age 11;[[37]](#cite_note-43) however, his father's health insurance covered only two years of the therapy, which cost at least 1,000 pesos per month. Newell's agreed to contribute, but later reneged on their promise.[[38]](#cite_note-44) Messi was scouted by the Buenos Aires club [River Plate](/wiki/Club_Atl%C3%A9tic

This article is about the contemporary list of wealthiest Americans. For a historical list, see [List of richest Americans in history](/wiki/List_of_richest_Americans_in_history "List of richest Americans in history").

This is a **list of the wealthiest Americans ranked by net worth**. It is based on an annual assessment of wealth and assets by *[Forbes](/wiki/Forbes "Forbes")* and by data from the [*Bloomberg Billionaires Index*](/wiki/Bloomberg_Billionaires_Index "Bloomberg Billionaires Index").

The [*Forbes* 400 Richest Americans](/wiki/Forbes_400_Richest_Americans "Forbes 400 Richest Americans") list has been published annually since 1982. The combined net worth of the 2020 class of the 400 richest Americans was $3.2 [trillion](/wiki/Trillion_(short_scale) "Trillion (short scale)"), up from $2.7 trillion in 2017.[[1]](#cite_note-Forbes400-2020-1) As of April 2025, there were 902 [billionaires](/wiki/Billionaire "Billionaire") in the United States.[[2]](#cite_note-2)

Jim Kenney :: Mayor of Philadelphia :: Second term (2020–2024) :: COVID-19 pandemic :: chunk_0008
In March 2020, Kenney declared [state of emergency](/wiki/State_of_emergency "State of emergency") amid the spread of [COVID-19 pandemic](/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic "COVID-19 pandemic"), caused by SARS-CoV-2. The pandemic has resulted in severe social and economic disruption around the world, including the largest global recession since the Great Depression in the 1930s. In Philadelphia, COVID has led to widespread supply shortages exacerbated by [panic buying](/wiki/Panic_buying "Panic buying"), agricultural disruption, and [food shortages](/wiki/Food_security "Food security"), as well as increased [gun violence](/wiki/Gun_violence "Gun violence"), opioid usage, and [housing insecurity](/wiki/Housing_insecurity "Housing insecurity"). Kenny has referred to COVID as a "[nuclear bomb](/wiki/Nuclear_bomb "Nuclear bomb")" because of the way it affected the city.[[41]](#cite_note-41)

See also: [Killing of Walter Wallace](/wiki/Killing_of_Walter_Wallace "Killing of Walter Wallace")

During the summer of 2020, Kenney approved the use of [CS gas](/wiki/CS_gas "CS gas") on protestors during a peaceful protest, who were blocking traffic, on [Interstate 676](/wiki/Interstate_676 "Interstate 676").[[42]](#cite_note-42)

In response to protests over the [murder of George Floyd](/wiki/Murder_of_George_Floyd "Murder of George Floyd"), Kenney had the Center City [statue](/wiki/Statue_of_Frank_Rizzo "Statue of Frank Rizzo") of [Frank Rizzo](/wiki/Frank_Rizzo "Frank Rizzo") removed in June 2020.[[43]](#cite_note-43)

Kenney was known for his outspoken feuds and reports on public figures or groups who attack his legislative agenda, image, or the city of Philadelphia. The **Yenisey** or **Yenisei**[[8]](#cite_note-:0-8) ([/ˌjɛnɪˈseɪ/](/wiki/Help:IPA/English "Help:IPA/English"), [*YEN-iss-AY*](/wiki/Help:Pronunciation_respelling_key "Help:Pronunciation respelling key"); [Russian](/wiki/Russian_language "Russian language"): Енисе́й, pronounced [[jɪnʲɪˈsʲej]](/wiki/Help:IPA/Russian "Help:IPA/Russian"))[[a]](#cite_note-10) is the [fifth-longest](/wiki/List_of_rivers_by_length "List of rivers by length") river system in the world, and the largest to drain into the [Arctic Ocean](/wiki/Arctic_Ocean "Arctic Ocean").

Rising in Mungaragiyn-gol in Mongolia, it follows a northerly course through [Lake Baikal](/wiki/Lake_Baikal "Lake Baikal") and the [Krasnoyarsk Dam](/wiki/Krasnoyarsk_Dam "Krasnoyarsk Dam") before draining into the [Yenisey Gulf](/wiki/Yenisey_Gulf "Yenisey Gulf") in the [Kara Sea](/wiki/Kara_Sea "Kara Sea"). The Yenisey divides the [Western Siberian Plain](/wiki/Western_Siberian_Plain "Western Siberian Plain") in the west from the [Central Siberian Plateau](/wiki/Central_Siberian_Plateau "Central Siberian Plateau") to the east; it drains a large part of central [Siberia](/wiki/Siberia "Siberia"). Its delta is formed between the [Gyda Peninsula](/wiki/Gyda_Peninsula "Gyda Peninsula") and the [Taymyr Peninsula](/wiki/Taymyr_Peninsula "Taymyr Peninsula").

It is the central one of three large Siberian rivers that flow into the [Arctic Ocean](/wiki/Arctic_Ocean "Arctic Ocean") (the other two being the [Ob](/wiki/Ob_(river) "Ob (river)") and the [Lena](/wiki/Lena_River "Lena River")). The maximum depth of the Yenisey is 61 metres (200 ft) and the average depth is 14 metres (45 ft).

fanoutqa_021766.t: Saitama Seibu Lions :: Franchise history :: Saitama Seibu Lions (2008–present) :: chunk_0009

Saitama Seibu Lions :: Franchise history :: Saitama Seibu Lions (2008–present) :: chunk_0009
In order to reinforce the affiliation between the team and their home region, the Lions added the prefecture name "Saitama" to their team name in 2008. They were Pacific League Champions that year and went on to win the [Japan Series](/wiki/2008_Japan_Series "2008 Japan Series"). The team logo and uniforms were further modified for the [2009 season](/wiki/2009_Nippon_Professional_Baseball_season "2009 Nippon Professional Baseball season"), with the team trading in their traditional light-blue colour scheme for a dark blue design similar to that employed during the Nishitetsu Lions era in the 1950s and 1960s. Between 2010 and 2019, the Lions made the Pacific League Climax Series 1st stage 5 times, (2010, 2011, 2012, 2013, 2017) but lost to the [Chiba Lotte Marines](/wiki/Chiba_Lotte_Marines "Chiba Lotte Marines") in 2010 and 2013, the [Tohoku Rakuten Golden Eagles](/wiki/Tohoku_Rakuten_Golden_Eagles "Tohoku Rakuten Golden Eagles") in 2017, and to the [Fukuoka SoftBank Hawks](/wiki/Fukuoka_SoftBank_Hawks "Fukuoka SoftBank Hawks") in 2011 and 2012. They made the Final Stage twice in back to back years in 2018 and 2019, but lost to the Hawks on both occasions. In 2020, the team finished in 3rd place, but was unable to make the playoffs. Due to the COVID-19 pandemic, the Pacific League removed the First Stage of the playoffs; only the top 2 teams in Pacific League made the playoffs, while Central League removed it entirely, instead opting to send the regular season champion ([Yomiuri Giants](/wiki/Yomiuri_Giants "Yomiuri Giants")) straight to the [Japan Series](/wiki/2020_Japan_Series "2020 Japan Series"). In 2021, the Lions finished in 6th and last place for the first time since 1979 with a 55–70–18 record.

fanoutqa_038406.x:
Arabian Desert :: Climate :: chunk_0002
The Arabian Desert has a [subtropical](/wiki/Subtropical "Subtropical"), [hot desert climate](/wiki/Hot_desert_climate "Hot desert climate"), similar to the climate of the [Sahara Desert](/wiki/Sahara_Desert "Sahara Desert") (the world's largest hot desert). The Arabian Desert is actually an extension of the Sahara Desert over the Arabian peninsula.

The climate is mainly dry. Most areas get around 100 mm (3.9 in) of rain per year. Unlike the Sahara Desert—more than half of which is [hyperarid](https://en.wiktionary.org/wiki/hyperarid#English "wiktionary:hyperarid") (having rainfall of less than 50 mm (2.0 in) per year)—the Arabian Desert has only a few hyperarid areas. These rare driest areas may get only 30 to 40 mm (1.6 in) of rain per year.

The Arabian Desert’s [sunshine duration](/wiki/Sunshine_duration "Sunshine duration") index is very high by global standards: between 2,900 hours (66.2% of daylight hours) and 3,600 hours (82.1% of daylight hours), but typically around 3,400 hours (77.6% of daylight hours). Thus clear-sky conditions with plenty of sunshine prevail over the region throughout the year, and cloudy periods are infrequent. Visibility at ground level is relatively low, despite the brightness of the sun and moon, because of dust and [humidity](/wiki/Humidity "Humidity").

Temperatures remain high year round. In the summer, in low-lying areas, average high temperatures are generally over 40 °C (104 °F). In extremely low-lying areas, especially along the Persian Gulf (near sea level), summer temperatures can reach 48 °C (118 °F). Average low temperatures in summer are typically over 20 °C (68 °F) and in the south can sometimes exceed 30 °C (86 °F). Record high temperatures above 50 °C (122 °F) have been reached in many areas of the desert, partly because its overall elevation is relatively low.
